A calm, consistent evening routine often helps with sleep: switch off screens 30–60 minutes beforehand, avoid caffeine in the evening and keep your wake-up time as regular as possible. Your sleep score: {{sleepScore}}.

Fitness is one of the most effective levers: even 3 × 20–30 minutes of brisk walking per week plus 2 short strength sessions can make a difference. Build up slowly and schedule fixed times. Your fitness score: {{fitnessScore}}.
Small changes can make a difference: add an extra portion of vegetables, pulses or whole grains each day and cut back on sweetened drinks. Your nutrition score: {{nutritionScore}}.

For healthy adults who strength-train regularly, around 1.4–1.6 g/kg/day is a practical guide. On average, the additional benefits for building lean body mass level off markedly at around 1.6 g/kg/day. Up to around 2.0 g/kg/day may be a reasonable individual range during very high training loads or a planned energy deficit. Most people do not need this amount, and age alone does not justify this target. People under 18, or anyone with kidney disease or a medically prescribed diet, should discuss the appropriate amount with a healthcare professional.

Specific values should be assessed by a doctor. I cannot and must not assess them. If your baseline values are unknown, it may be useful to have your blood pressure, blood glucose/HbA1c and blood lipids measured when convenient.

The Helsana Coach app helps you stay on track each day with plans, reminders and exercises. With your consent, your profile (score, focus areas and next steps) could be transferred directly. You will find the link further down this page.
